# Exact obstruction to every single-outer high-core circuit

Research draft, 6 November 2026. This is a convex-body counterexample to a proposed arithmetic reservoir implication, not to OC. It also supplies a low-target repair mechanism.

## Complete source census

Fix n,d>=1 and a d-body K with centroid zero and volume V. Let 0<t<1, delta=t^d, sigma=((1+t)/2)^d, and

    P={0,1}^n, G=P minus {0}, O={-e_1,...,-e_n},
    C=conv((G x K) union (O x tK)).

The integer bases of C are exactly P union O. Every coordinate of a projected point lies in [-1,1]. A coordinate equal to -1 forces the point to be the unique negative generator -e_i attaining that value. An integer point without a negative coordinate lies in P. All nonzero P points are generators, and 0 is the midpoint of e_i and -e_i. This proves the entire integer-base census.

Every fiber at G is K: it already contains K and all continuous generators lie in K. Every fiber at -e_i is tK, because that base is uniquely exposed by its ith coordinate. At base zero the fiber is exactly ((1+t)/2)K. Indeed if lambda is the total coefficient of positive generators, applying the coordinate-sum functional gives lambda<=1-lambda, since that sum is at least1 on G and equals-1 on O. Therefore the continuous coordinate lies in [lambda+(1-lambda)t]K subset ((1+t)/2)K. The midpoint of e_i and -e_i gives equality. The body is compact, convex and full-dimensional.

Consequently, with L=2^n,

    E=n delta V,
    W=(L-1+sigma+n delta)V,
    B_avg=W/L=V[1+(n delta-(1-sigma))/L].                (1)

The complete parity core P is an empty lattice polytope in convex position; its high subset G is also in convex position and lattice convex. Every outer base -e_i has same-parity core partner e_i and reflected middle0. There is exactly one outer fiber in each of these n parity classes. The maximum outer parity mass is delta V. The pointwise smallness condition max_outer volume<2^{-d}min_core volume holds whenever delta<2^{-d}sigma; for example t<=1/4 suffices strictly.

For any fixed sufficiently small t and eta>0 with sigma<1/(1+eta), choose n so large that n delta>1-sigma and n delta/2^n<eta. Then B_avg>V, so the largest-fiber bound Gamma V is below the sharp target Gamma B_avg. Nevertheless every nonzero core is eta-good, there is only one bad core, and all outside mass targets that bad core.

## All individual-outer high-core reservoirs vanish

For every w in G, p in O and beta in (0,1], there is no representation

    w=beta p+(1-beta)c,
    c in conv(G minus {w}).                              (2)

Choose a coordinate j with w_j=1. Every p in O has p_j<=0, whereas every c in conv(G minus {w}) has c_j<=1. The right-hand side in that coordinate is therefore at most1-beta<1, contradiction. For beta=1 the contradiction is immediate as well.

Thus R_w(b)=0 for every high w and every b<1, even with no upper restriction on circuit arity. All good-good reflected-pair credits also vanish: every outer midpoint is the single bad core0. The source can have arbitrarily small individual and per-parity outer masses, an arbitrarily small fraction of bad core vertices, and failure of the largest-fiber bound. Hence those hypotheses do not force the proposed arithmetic reservoir. An additional consequence of failed OC must enter.

## A stronger low-center certificate repairs this family

Write Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d. The actual point (0,0) has depth at least

    Gamma(sigma+n delta)V.                               (3)

To see this, take a closed ambient halfspace through (0,0). The actual endpoint centroids at (e_i,0) and (-e_i,0) have midpoint (0,0), so at least one belongs to the halfspace. If the positive endpoint centroid belongs, its actual fiber contributes at least Gamma V>=Gamma delta V by ordinary Grünbaum. Otherwise the negative endpoint centroid belongs and its fiber contributes at least Gamma delta V. All n endpoint pairs are physically disjoint. The middle centroid contributes at least Gamma sigma V. Pure integer halfspaces contain whole selected fibers and satisfy the same inequalities. Summing proves (3), and containing halfspaces reduce to through-point halfspaces by inclusion.

If n delta<=1-sigma, (1) gives B_avg<=V and a high-fiber centroid proves sharp OC. If n delta>=1-sigma, set Q=sigma+n delta>=1; then W/V=(L-1)+Q<=LQ. Thus (3) proves sharp OC. The stronger low-center bound reaches the target precisely when Q>=1, the complement of the largest-fiber regime.

## General pair-centroid compatibility lemma

Let an actual middle fiber B at w have centroid g and volume v. Let distinct actual endpoint pairs A_i at p_i and C_i at z_i satisfy p_i+z_i=2w, with all endpoint bases distinct from each other and from w. Let a_i,c_i be their volumes and g_Ai,g_Ci their true centroids. If

    (g_Ai+g_Ci)/2=g for every i,

then

    h_C(w,g)>=Gamma[v+sum_i min(a_i,c_i)].                (4)

The proof is exactly the pairwise halfspace argument above; no global affine centroid map is needed. This includes oblique and pure integer cuts.

If (A_i+C_i)/2 subset B and

    |B|=((a_i^{1/d}+c_i^{1/d})/2)^d                      (5)

for every i, equality in Brunn-Minkowski makes A_i,C_i homothetic, and equality of the containing volumes identifies their midpoint body with B. The centroid of a Minkowski sum of homothetic bodies is the corresponding sum of their centroids, so (5) implies the compatibility hypothesis of (4). For d=1 the same assertion follows directly from interval endpoints. Equality of full-dimensional compact convex bodies under inclusion and equal volume is exact; no boundary-only discrepancy remains.

Suppose there are L positive-volume core fibers including B, the A_i are precisely all positive-volume outside fibers, each C_i is a core fiber, and the displayed disjoint pairs are centered about the one core w. Assume a_i<=c_i. Let M be the largest core volume and E=sum_i a_i. The largest-core centroid gives Gamma M, while (4) gives Gamma(v+E). Since

    W<= (L-1)M+v+E <=L max(M,v+E),

one of these two actual points has depth at least Gamma W/L. For a complete parity core L=2^n this is the sharp OC constant on this centroid-compatible star class.

The exact BM-saturation hypothesis (5) is sufficient, not necessary. The transport-deficit companion note replaces it by an explicit linear penalty for excess middle volume, with arbitrary endpoint shapes.
statement: Cube-minus-origin obstruction to all single-outer high-core circuits. Exact hypotheses, definitions, constants and scope are given in the proof text. This does not assert the unrestricted weak or sharp Oertel conjecture.
